title: Нагиев замечает поваров в зале  (Nagiyev Spots the Cooks on the Floor)

segments.t: Spotting Senya, Fedya, and Lyova carrying plates across the dining room floor right in front of the visiting film director, a horrified Nagiyev excuses himself from the table. He pulls Vika and Chef Barinov aside and is outraged to learn that the waitresses never showed up for their shift.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'What on earth are the cooks doing in the dining room?' Addressing the cook with Lyova, Barinov puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Lyova hears the focus immediately.
'What is the meaning of this?' Lyova prompts briskly where this conversation is heading next.

'The cooks are personally bringing out what they prepared.' Underscoring the cook beside Lyova, Barinov lands on "prigotovili" ("cooked, prepared", built on "prigotovit") to keep the statement grounded.
'What the hell are you people doing, huh?' Looking over warmly right here, Lyova puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Barinov hears the focus immediately.
'We will fix everything right now.' Barinov counters promptly without any doubt, before Lyova can change the subject.
'So to speak.' Turning evenly beside Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Follow me, right now.' Weighing in candidly before Lyova, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'What is going on in our restaurant?' Lyova questions wryly whether Barinov really thought this through.
'They did not show up for work today.' Barinov follows up plainly to Lyova and lands on "segodnya" ("today") as the key everyday word here.
'What do you mean, they did not show up?' Opening up smoothly on the spot, Lyova puts the question word "kak" right at the start so Barinov hears the focus immediately.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
'You do not even know where your own subordinates are?' Barinov asks promptly what Lyova is actually getting at here.
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
'Do you know what that says about you, huh?' Lyova jumps in briskly during the talk and chooses "govorit" ("talks") so Barinov gets the point right away.
'And you know, the old man is right.' Emphasizing how right things are during the talk, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?

That wraps up this scene as stunned to see line cooks serving tables in front of the film director, Nagiyev drags Chef Barinov and Vika aside and learns that none of the waitresses came to work. See you next time!
